components.css: .ds-track { height: 40px; display: flex; border-bottom: 1px solid #242a24; background: #0c0f0d; font-family: "YTA Source", "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-track-label { width: 112px; min-width: 112px; display: grid; place-items: center; border-right: 1px solid #343d34; color: #8f988c; background: #111511; font-family: "YTA Condensed", sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.045em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-track-content { position: relative; flex: 1; overflow: hidden; background-color: #090b09; background-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent calc(100% - 1px), rgba(105, 117, 103, 0.1)); background-size: 80px 100%; } .ds-timeline-clip { position: absolute; inset: 3px auto 3px 12px; width: 190px; display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 8px; border: 1px solid var(--primary, #c6f36a); border-radius: 4px; color: #dfe8d6; background: #334326; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(198, 243, 106, 0.18); font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; cursor: grab; transition: box-shadow 150ms ease, filter 150ms ease; } .ds-timeline-clip:hover { filter: brightness(1.15); } .ds-timeline-clip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary, #c6f36a); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-playhead { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: 238px; width: 1px; background: var(--warning, #ffb454); } .ds-playhead::before { position: absolute; top: 0; left: -4px; border: 4px solid transparent; border-top-color: var(--warning, #ffb454); content: ""; }

narrative.overview:
Cut Ledger treats YTA Empire as an edit decision ledger rather than a generic dashboard. Matte carbon bays frame a dominant program monitor; warm paper text, ruled timecode, and sharply divided tracks make automation legible as an editing process.

The interface is dense, restrained, and operational. Lime is reserved for selection and primary action, amber marks processing and the current time, and quiet carbon layers preserve context across import, build, inspection, refinement, and render.

The independent finish review disposition is PASS across THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, and FORM.
keyCharacteristics: Matte carbon editing-console surfaces with warm paper text.
Condensed uppercase bay labels paired with compact humanist body copy.
Ruled timecode, fixed track labels, and 80px timeline divisions.
Lime selection and primary actions; amber processing and playhead states.
Tight desktop density with shallow radii, hairline borders, and selective structural shadow.

rules.name: The Signal Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Lime means selection and primary action; amber means processing or current time; green means healthy status; coral means fault or destructive state.

rules.name: The Matte Majority Rule
rules.body: Carbon surfaces dominate every viewport; accent colors stay local to state, selection, and action.

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Condensed names the workspace, Source explains and controls it, and Consolas reports time or machine state.

rules.name: The Context-Preservation Rule
rules.body: Responsive changes remove secondary header information before hiding editing state, the monitor, inspector, or timeline.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Needed Rule
rules.body: Panels, cards, and clips are flat at rest; shadow appears only when a surface must separate spatially or capture active input.

rules.name: The Shallow-Corner Rule
rules.body: Keep operational surfaces between 4px and 10px; reserve pills and circles for badges, status, and icon-only controls.

rules.name: The State-Before-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Every accent, border shift, and shadow must communicate selection, progress, health, error, hierarchy, or input focus.

dos: Do keep Matte Carbon, Console Carbon, and Track Black as the visual majority.
Do use Selection Lime for the active edit target, primary action, checked control, and keyboard focus.
Do use Processing Amber for build progress, agent progress, and the current-time playhead.
Do preserve the dominant program monitor, visible side bays, and ruled timeline in desktop layouts.
Do use condensed uppercase labels for bays, tracks, and technical toolbar metadata.
donts: Don't reintroduce purple gradients, neon dashboard glows, or generic SaaS-card styling into the editor shell.
Don't use lime and amber interchangeably; they encode different operational states.
Don't float every section as a rounded card; panel structure comes from edge-to-edge stacking and hairline rules.
Don't hide essential editing context merely to simplify a narrower desktop viewport.
Don't add marketing claims, decorative data, or interface states that are not supported by the product.
